text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu says the peace process is not lost; Syrian President Assad says peace doors closed.
- Assad says Syria will give up "other weapons" when Israel gives up nuclear weapons.
- Netanyahu says Israel following flow of weapons to Iran and Syria and that it has an answer.
- Netanyahu sets up another ministerial forum; ministers complain Netanyahu setting up "kitchen cabinets" too fast.
- Revolution in Britain.
- New foriegn ministry "file" collecting documents on possibility of war with Syria.
- Grandchildren of SS officers and those of Holocaust survivors work together on collecting data for Israel's National Holocaust memorial Yad VaShem.
MAARIV
- Assad: When Israel gives up nuclear weapons we'll talk about chemical weapons; Netanyahu says Israel monitoring Syria and Iran weapon flow and it has an answer.
- Revolution in Britain.
- Majority of 51 percent back commission of inquiry into influence peddling scandal shadowing Netanyahu; 46 percent oopose; three percent don't know.
- Trade and Industry Minister Sharansky wants justice minister dismissed.
- Sources in Foreign Ministry say Netanyahu torpedoed Foreign Minister Levy's meeting with U.S. Secretary of State; Netanyahu's office rejects charge.
- Senior managers in economy asked to grade government officials and Bank of Israel governor; Netanyahu comes in last.
JERUSALEM POST
- Australian animal study links cell phone use to cancer.
- U.S. peace envoy to return.
- Blair sweeps to huge victory in UK.
- Kaplan quits Africa Israel; cites Leviev hands-on style.
- VAT chief favours near term tax hike.
- Israel mogul Eisenberg's will excludes daughter.
- Elbit in Brazil avionics deal.
- Assad: Whoever has nuclear weapons has no right to criticise others.
- Morale low among air force officers over report on helicopter accident in which more than 70 Israeli soldiers died; some officers want to resign.
- Blair victory.
- Treasury suggests reducing health services.
- Study: those from Asia and African countries in Israel more interested in education than those from West.
GLOBES
- Avigdor Kaplan to be appointed managing director of Clal Insurance.
- Surprise budget surplus of 472 million shekels ($1=3.41 shekels) in April.
